ecological_question: Are species with narrower independently compiled breeding seasons more strongly recruited into the acoustically active assemblage under wetter matched conditions?

response_source.response: pair-covariate-adjusted per-species wet-versus-dry intercept log odds

computational_transport.provenance: Derived from raw ATraiU_full_2020AUG.csv; the transport repository keeps the modal non-null breeding-season description for each species.

parser.allowed_information: explicit month names or three-letter month abbreviations only
parser.range_rule: Recognize explicit month-to-month ranges separated by '-', 'to', or 'through'; include all months inclusively. If end month precedes start month, wrap across December.
parser.standalone_rule: Any explicit month mention outside a recognized range is included as that month.
parser.multiple_ranges: Take union of all months recovered from all explicit ranges/mentions.
parser.season_words: Do not translate spring/summer/fall/autumn/winter or vague early/mid/late phrases into months.
parser.invalid: If no explicit month is recoverable, breeding-season breadth is missing.
parser.output: number of distinct calendar months represented, 1-12

primary_hypothesis.rationale: More episodic/narrow-breeding species should depend more strongly on short rainfall opportunities and therefore show more positive wet-recruitment responses.

primary_model.estimator: inverse-variance weighted least squares with HC3 covariance across species

family_structure_sensitivity.method: weighted within-family slope after subtracting weighted family means from predictor and response
family_structure_sensitivity.permutation: permute breeding-season breadth among species within family
family_structure_sensitivity.inferential_role: robustness only; not required for primary association

exact_group_descriptive.definition: short-season <=3 parsed months versus long-season >=6 parsed months
exact_group_descriptive.status: descriptive only; thresholds frozen before readback

boundaries: Breeding-season breadth is a phenological proxy, not a direct measure of explosive breeding.
The source uses a modal breeding-season description after collapsing references; intraspecific geographic variation is not represented comprehensively.
This is a post-opening mechanistic follow-up and not an original preregistered hypothesis.
No additional ATraiU traits may be promoted within this analysis family.
